limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on the earliest phase of organoid development (up to 120h) and may not capture later stages of maturation.
Causal claims are based on correlations and perturbation experiments; direct mechanistic proof of the Yap1-Notch/Dll1 switch may require further validation.
Some experiments were repeated only once (e.g., 4i multiplexing, certain stainings), limiting statistical power.
The role of other pathways interacting with Yap1/Notch is not explored.
Organoid formation efficiency assays were normalized to controls, but absolute efficiencies are not reported.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

claims.statement: Variability in nuclear Yap1 initiates a Notch/Dll1 lateral inhibition event: cells with high nuclear Yap1 become Dll1+ and subsequently Paneth cells, after which Yap1 regulation of Dll1 is lost.

provenance.text_excerpt: When we correlated the expression levels of the early expressed genes (24h vs 0h) in organoid development with the expression levels of Yap1-dependent gene expression 28, we observed a good correlation (r=0.45) (Fig. 3f).

From these findings, we conclude that during the first 72h of organoid development, Yap1 is transiently active in every cell and induces cell proliferation, after which it becomes inactive in only few cells. Both, homogeneous inactivation and overactivation of Yap1 in spheres abolish symmetry breaking and organoid formation suggesting that it is not the absolute levels of Yap1, but its varying state between single cells that drives symmetry breaking.

claims.statement: Yap1 is transiently active in every cell during the first 72h, inducing proliferation, and then becomes inactive in a subset of cells; both homogeneous inactivation and overactivation abolish symmetry breaking, indicating that variability in Yap1 state between cells drives symmetry breaking.
